title: The First Promise Of The Gospel

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel." — Gen 3:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Right here, in the middle of judgment, a light breaks through. God is still speaking to the serpent — but suddenly these words are no longer only about defeat for the tempter. They are about hope for humanity. Many believers across the centuries have called this verse the very first announcement of the Gospel, and rightly so.

God promises ongoing conflict — "enmity" — between the serpent and the woman, and between their offspring. History will be a long struggle between evil and the line of promise. But the outcome is already declared. One particular offspring of the woman "will crush your head." The serpent may "strike his heel" — a real wound, but not a fatal one. The head-crushing blow, however, is final.

Think of how beautifully this points forward. At the cross, it looked as though the serpent had won — the heel was struck, the Saviour wounded, laid in a tomb. But that very wound became the serpent's undoing. Through His death and resurrection, Jesus crushed the head of the enemy and broke the power of sin and death forever (Heb 2:14). What was promised in the garden was fulfilled at Calvary.

Dear friend, hold onto this. From the earliest pages of the Bible, God had already set His rescue in motion. Before Adam and Eve took a single step out of Eden, grace had spoken. The story of the whole Bible — the coming of Christ to defeat evil and save sinners — begins right here.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it encourage you that God announced His rescue plan in the very moment of judgment?
2. Where do you need to remember that a present wound is not the same as final defeat?
3. How does it change your view of the cross to see it foretold from the beginning?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that even in the garden, before the door of Eden closed, You had already promised a Saviour. Thank You that Jesus crushed the enemy's head through His death and resurrection. Help me to live in the hope of that finished victory today. Amen.
